hero.headline: When fire is on the news, know what it means for your home.
hero.lede: Fire Watch is an autonomous fire analyst. It reads the satellites, the official incident feeds, and the fire weather — then answers the only question that matters: is this a threat to your address, and what should you do next?
hero.verdictNote: Every briefing leads with one of four verdicts — and the single driver behind it. Traffic lights, not decimal probabilities.

report.title: One report. Verdict first.
report.lede: A briefing built for the anxious person at 11pm who just saw fire coverage on the news — the verdict comes first, the reasoning second, and nothing pretends to more precision than the data supports.

deliverables.title: The verdict and its driver
deliverables.text: Green, Yellow, Orange, or Red — with the single factor that put it there, in plain language.

deliverables.title: Threat map and geometry
deliverables.text: Every relevant fire plotted against your address, with distance and wind alignment — because the threat is where fire will be, not where it is.

deliverables.title: Five-dimension risk scores
deliverables.text: Active-fire threat, fire weather, fuel load, property vulnerability, and escape routes — each scored 1–5, honestly, gaps included.

deliverables.title: Actions and triggers
deliverables.text: At most three actions sized to the level, plus the explicit conditions that would escalate or downgrade the verdict.

report.delivery: Delivered as a PDF and your own report web page. Every figure traces back to a stored evidence bundle — the report tells you which one.

example.label: Read the example briefing
example.note: A real report for the operator's own home near Lisbon, generated 29 July 2026.

data.title: Official feeds, satellites, and fire weather — fetched once, stored auditable.
data.lede: One national data sweep feeds every assessment. Nothing is hand-picked, and every number in your report can be checked against the evidence bundle recorded at run time.

sources.name: IPMA RCM
sources.detail: Portugal's official fire-danger index for your municipality, on a 1–5 scale, refreshed hourly by the national weather institute.

sources.name: NASA FIRMS
sources.detail: VIIRS and MODIS thermal hotspots, confidence-filtered. Typically 1–4 hours behind reality — the report says so instead of hiding it.

sources.name: National incident feed
sources.detail: Every active wildfire in Portugal with crews, vehicles, and aircraft committed — which also powers the suppression-strain signal: how stretched the national response already is.

sources.name: Fire weather
sources.detail: High-resolution IPMA forecasts. Red-flag combinations — dry, hot, windy — elevate the risk score regardless of how far the nearest fire is.

sources.name: EFFIS
sources.detail: The EU's calibrated fire-weather scale, used as forecast context on top of the national danger rating.

sources.name: MeteoAlarm
sources.detail: The official European channel for heat and wind warnings issued by national authorities.

data.note: Detection latency, degraded sources, and data gaps are stated in the report, never papered over. If a layer is down, the briefing says which one and what that does to confidence.

method.title: A sensor and an analyst — separated on purpose.
method.lede: Risk is scored by a deterministic engine, then interpreted by an analyst layer. The same inputs always produce the same verdict; judgment is added on top, never smuggled in.

engine.title: The engine senses and scores
points: Fetches all sources and stores the raw evidence in an auditable bundle.
Scores five risk dimensions and combines them with fixed weights.
Applies hard override rules — a close, upwind fire forces the level up no matter what the average says.

analyst.title: The analyst interprets
points: Reads the threat as a trajectory: where fire will be given wind, fuel, and slope — wind alignment before distance.
Writes the narrative and the actions in plain language, at the reader's level.
May disagree with the computed level — but only in a clearly labeled analyst note, never silently.

principles.title: Verdict first
principles.text: The color and its driver lead every output. Reasoning follows for those who want it.

principles.title: No false precision
principles.text: Four levels, honest gaps, stated assumptions. Decimal probabilities don't help you decide whether to load the car.

principles.title: Auditable
principles.text: A claim like “0 incidents within 60 km” is checkable against the evidence bundle recorded for that exact run.

flow.title: Message the agent. Answer a few questions. Get your briefing.
flow.lede: The whole exchange happens in a chat with the agent itself — there is no form on this page.

steps.title: Message the agent
steps.text: Reach out on Telegram. You'll be asked to verify who you are.

steps.title: Get approved
steps.text: Access is personal: every requester is approved by the operator before any report runs.

steps.title: Answer a few questions
steps.text: The agent asks for your address or coordinates in Portugal — and optionally your structure type, cleared distance around the house, and escape routes. Defaults are used and stated if you skip them.

steps.title: Receive your briefing
steps.text: A plain-language summary in the chat, the PDF, and a link to your own report page. The report is a snapshot, valid as of its timestamp — you can request a refresh any time.

contact.title: Talk to the agent
contact.text: One channel, one capability: request a fire-risk briefing for an address in Portugal.
